title: Django Docker GUI
subtitle: Docker Management Interface
description: A web UI for Docker images and containers, with a real terminal in the browser. Telepy's great-grandparent, in spirit.
longDescription: A powerful web-based interface for managing Docker containers and images, featuring a fully functional terminal emulator. This tool provides system administrators and developers with an intuitive way to manage Docker environments through a web browser.
mascotLines: Every account is a superuser. Hand them out like root passwords.
Docker commands are easy, as long as you remember the container ID.
imageCaptions: A shell in the nginx container, opened from the browser. Even 你好 comes out right.
Docker Hub search for redis, with star counts, an Official badge and Pull buttons.
One web container holds the Docker socket; Redis carries the jobs and their events.
One console session, from opening the WebSocket to kill -HUP when you close the tab.
why: Docker's command line is fine as long as you remember the container ID. This page lists them for you, puts start, stop and pull behind buttons, and opens a real shell in any container from the browser. It began as a refactor of MahmoudAlyy's docker-django-ui.
gains: Handy for one person or a small trusted team on one machine: restart, pull or open a shell from a browser tab, even in Alpine images that have no bash. Every account is a superuser by design, so hand out logins the way you'd hand out root.
lessons: Docker has no call to end an exec'd shell, and one left behind keeps running, so the shell writes its PID first and closing the tab sends it kill -HUP.
Browsers can't add headers to WebSockets, so the login token rides along as a token.<base64> subprotocol.
Any Console can reach the container holding the Docker socket, so smaller roles would be theatre: only active superusers get in, checked in one file.
